recommendation.recommendation: Conduct an immediate, comprehensive field inspection to diagnose disease presence and nutrient deficiencies, and assess soil erosion risk.
recommendation.justification: Satellite data shows critical vegetation health (NDVI < 0.30) and high soil exposure (SAVI < 0.25), indicating severe canopy loss and erosion risk. While soil quality and water availability are optimal, the risk of anthracnose, powdery mildew, and nutrient imbalance could cause significant yield loss if not addressed promptly.
actions: Schedule an on‑site inspection within the next 48 hours (owner: Agronomist).
Visually inspect canopy for symptoms of anthracnose (black spots) and powdery mildew (white powder).
Collect leaf samples from symptomatic and healthy trees for laboratory nutrient analysis (N, P, K).
Walk the orchard perimeter to identify signs of soil erosion or surface runoff linked to high SAVI values.
If disease is confirmed, apply the recommended fungicide according to label rates (e.g., copper‑based for anthracnose, sulfur‑based for powdery mildew).
Based on nutrient test results, adjust fertilization: apply NPK 10:10:10 at 200 kg ha⁻¹ split into two applications, supplement with compost/manure to maintain high organic carbon.
Record all observations, treatments, and soil measurements in the farm management log.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Early detection and treatment will halt canopy decline, reduce disease spread, correct nutrient imbalances, and prevent erosion, thereby preserving yield potential and maintaining profitability for the upcoming May‑July harvest.
monitoring_plan: Weekly NDVI tracking via satellite or drone imagery to verify canopy recovery.
Bi‑weekly visual scouting for disease symptoms after treatment.
Monthly leaf nutrient re‑testing until levels are within optimal ranges.
Soil surface inspections after each rain event to monitor erosion.
Adjust irrigation (drip, every 7‑10 days) as needed based on NDWI readings.
